Messages.Body:
umm.. . well this is my first deck and I made it based on the
Disciplines of Protean and Fortitude. The theme I was trying to go for
was this, I horde blood and I get my vampire out quick...hmm...I'm not
sure that came out right...oh well heres the deck... ^_^

Vampires

The Fourth Tradition: The Accounting - 2 (note - is this card a master
ot did they screw up when printing it???)
The Fifth Tradition: Hospitality - 2

Rapid Healing - 2

Grenade - 2

---------

Skin of Rock - 4
Skin of Steel - 4
Wolf Claws - 4
Lucky Blow - 2
Fake Out - 2
Boxed In - 2
Blood Rage - 2

Well thats it... what do you all think?? One thing though, if you do

Bill

Messages.Author: TheLa...@hotmail.com
Messages.Body:
In article <37008216...@columbus.rr.com>,

wlag...@columbus.rr.com wrote:
> umm.. . well this is my first deck and I made it based on the
> Disciplines of Protean and Fortitude. The theme I was trying to go for
> was this, I horde blood and I get my vampire out quick...hmm...I'm not
> sure that came out right...oh well heres the deck... ^_^
>
> Vampires
> -----------
>
> Roman Alexander - 4 cap pro/for/ani
> Ricki Van Demsy - 3 cap pro/for
> Anastasia Grey - 3 cap pro/ani
> Gitane St. Claire - 7 cap PRO/FOR/ANI - primogen
> Gunther - Beast Lord - 7 cap - aus/pro/for/ANI
> Bear Paw - 5 cap pro/pre/for/ANI
> Zack North - 6 cap dom/pro/for/ani
> Badger - 6 cap ani/dom/PRO/FOR
> Camille Devereux - 5 cap ani/PRO/FOR
> Angus - The Unruled - 10 cap cel/dom/for/PRO/ANI - gangrel justicar

For 10 pool, you should at least get both disciplines at superior.
Drop Angus.

> Basilia - 10 cap dom/obf/PRO/FOR/ANI - primogen
> Quinton McDonnell - 8 cap cel/pro/ani/FOR

For 8 pool you should at least get both disciplines at superior.
Drop Quinton.

As a general rule, when spending 6 or more pool on a vampire they
should have all of the disciplines that you are planning to use at
superior. Double up on the vampires that have both at superior,
Camille, Badger, Gitane. If you really have to go higher than 6, you
need to get a lot of benefit from their special abilities and that
vampires you have chosen aren't very special.

You only have to have 12 cards in your crypt not 12 unique vampires.
A number of very successful decks have been made with only 4-6 different
vampires with multiple copies of each in the crypt but only one copy of
each vampire in play.

>
> Total Vampires: 12 Total Blood: 74 Avg. Blood: 6.1
>
> Master
> --------

As you can only play 1 per turn, you should never go above 16-20
without also playing other cards that let you play them more often.
Most games will last 10-12 turns max once you and your opponents are
comfortable with the game.

> Ascendance - 4
> Gird Minions - 2

Get rid of this card. Vampires can hunt. That is what they should
do to regain blood, in very few situations should you ever want to put
blood back on them from your pool.

> Minion Tap - 2
> Elder Library - 1
> Effective Management - 2
> Protracted Investment - 4

Get rid of these and fast. It takes 4 turns to gain a profit
from playing this card during which time you play zero other
master cards. Unless you are playing with Anson (Toreador) this
card should not even be considered for your deck.

> Short Term Investment - 4

Either get rid of the Ascendances or the STI's. I would get
rid of the Ascendances because you don't have any long term
gain from them but you only gain 1 more from the STI's and
you have to pay a pool to bring them into play.

Remember, you cannot play another master card if you pull a
blood off of an investment card. I would recommend Blood Dolls
over all the cards that I have mentioned so far. They allow
you to regain pool, put pool on vampires if necessary and don't
take up the master phase actions on other turns.

A game winning tactic is to have a small vamp or two with Blood
Dolls hunting every turn to constantly bring blood back into your
pool, which you can then use to bring out more vampires. Eventually,
your predator or prey will start trying to block these hunting actions
but hunting is at +1 stealth so it will not be easy for them.

> Protean - 2
> Fortitude - 2
> Information Highway - 2
> Zoo Hunting Ground - 1
> Eco Terrorists - 1
> Backways - 1
>
> Total: 28
>
> Action
> --------
>
> Restoration - 4
> The Fourth Tradition: The Accounting - 2 (note - is this card a master

> or did they screw up when printing it???)

Yes, they screwed up printing it. It is an action card not a master card.

> The Fifth Tradition: Hospitality - 2

You only have 1 vampire that can play the 4th or the 5th Tradition
and I recommended earlier that you yank him. Yank these 4 cards as well.

> Ritual Challenge - 1
> Movement of the Slow Body - 2
> Rapid Healing - 2

You certainly seem to plan on going to torpor a lot. Without some
way of reliably going to torpor (Day Operation) I would probably
remove these and use just about anything else. Computer Hacking
for example. As the point of the game is to remove the opponents
pool, cards that help you do that will help speed up your deck,
and Speed is Good (TM).

> Total: 13
>
> Action Mod.
> --------------
>
> Freak Drive - 2
> Earth Control - 2
>
> Total: 4
>
> P. Action
> ------------
>
> Consanguineous Boon - 2

With only two vote cards and only 3 vampires with votes, these
will almost never pass in anything but a 2 player game. Ditch them
or add more vote gaining cards like Gangrel Justicar or any of the
Praxis Seizure cards.

> Total: 2
>
> Equipment
> -------------
>
> Hawg - 2
> Grenade - 2
> Ivory Bow - 1
> IR Goggles - 3

As a general rule equipment is too slow to bother with.
Keep the Ivory Bow because long range aggravated damage is always
a good thing but the rest should go and should be replaced with
Protean combat cards. Unless you are doing the running away
(maneuvering to long) IR Goggles will be a wasted action for you.

> Total: 8
>
> Combat
> ---------
>
> Skin of Night - 2
> Skin of Rock - 4
> Skin of Steel - 4
> Wolf Claws - 4
> Lucky Blow - 2
> Fake Out - 2

Get rid of Fake Out and replace with Form of the Ghost. Replacing
cards is essential to a good combat deck (or any other deck really).
More below.

> Boxed In - 2

Get rid of this and put in Gleam of the Red Eyes for your presses.
You want to be able to cycle your cards as much as possible. It is
better to replace that press card and draw your Lucky Blow than it
is to play your press and be with 6 cards until the end of combat.

> Blood Rage - 2

Blood Rage was misprinted. It is a thaumaturgy strike
not a fortitude strike. Take it out.

> Body of Sun - 1
> Earth Meld - 4
> Claws of the Dead - 4
> Indomitability - 4
>
> Total: 35

You know of course that officially there is no card limit in Jyhad.
You may have more than 4 of every card in your deck. I assume that
most of your limits are going to be from simply not having more
rather than anything else, but thought I might remind you anyway.

If you want to use equipment, Laptop Computers are much better than
the combat based ones you have chosen. With your Wolf Claws and Claws
of the Dead, you won't see combat reach a second round more often
than not because your opponent will be in torpor (unless they can
avoid your damage by preventing or dodging). A last reminder, the
point of the game is to remove your prey's pool. Things that help
you do that are good and things that don't should be carefully
considered.

Carpe Noctem.

Lasombra

Well, let`s remember the basic things of deck building:

1st: You want to oust your prey. After you ousted your prey, you want to
oust your next prey. After that you want to continue ousting until you
won.

2nd: To win all those victory points, you have to be fast enough to get
them before someone else accumulates too much victory points. Speed is
important.

3rd: You have to make sure that you can pursue your strategy by an
effective tactic: it mustn`t be luck which wins you the game (at least,
not always)

So if you play with FOR PRO, try to use the most cost efficient vamps
with those disciplines:

Camille Devereux
Badger
Gitane St. Claire
Raven (the V:TES replacement for Camille)

and some weenies as supporting bleeders / rescue teams. This makes sure
that you have the disciplines you need for a decent pool cost, and you
can act fast enough to damage your prey.

A sample (Jyhad-only) crypt might be:

3x Camille Devereux
3x Badger
3x Gitane St. Claire
1x Igo the Hungry
1x Guliano Vincenci
1x Ricky van Demsi

IMHO the best strategy for PRO FOR is rush & bleed, so you want to first
strike your enemies into submission and then bleed your prey into
nothingness.

A nice tactic could be to (Bum`s) Rush them first, beat the enemy vamps
into torpor, freak drive, equip with a Laptop, freak drive, bleed with
Computer Hacking. (Skip the Laptop if you want)

The problem is one of the most common anti-combat defenses: Strike :
Combat ends.

To cope with this, you need Animalism (work with Animalism master cards)

Tactic would be now:

Bleed with (Laptop &) Computer Hacking
if they don`t block - well, fine.
if they block, you play
Dawn Operation (damage in combat is aggro)
Drawing out the Beast (superior version)
Strike: Form of Mist or Earth Meld (superior version)
(Effect: At the end of combat, your enemy takes 1 unpreventable aggro
damage and you continue with your action / untap)
Of course you best have a Skin of Steel in your hand, just in case
someone wants to immortally grapple you (so you have to use hand
strikes)

Or you work with Potence, using Immortal Grapple yourself (basic potence
is sufficient)

Bum`s Rush, Drawing out the beast (to keep them at close range),
Immortal Grapple (no combat ends, no dodge, just hand strikes), Wolf
Claws for some aggro damage and Skin of Steel to prevent enemy strike
damage.

Of course, all strike tactics may be combined with the Undead
Persistence + Movement of the slow body + Rapid healing combination of
cards, but - remember: those actions may be blocked.

Michael Beer

>If you want to use equipment, Laptop Computers are much better than
>the combat based ones you have chosen. With your Wolf Claws and Claws
>of the Dead, you won't see combat reach a second round more often
>than not because your opponent will be in torpor (unless they can
>avoid your damage by preventing or dodging).

Disagree slightly. HtH decks do need some way to close the range in combat,
as we have seen from another recent thread people playing weenie presence
bleed prefer to mix their majesties and fake outs.
For the Gangrel the card of choice is Drawing out the Beast, so that there
is no possibility of being defeated in a maneuver contest, this also stops
the opposing minion using equipment. However, you may not always have the
DotB in your hand/may run out, so equipping your vampire with a permanent
maneuver is not a bad thing. I would recommend shadow of the beast for a
gangrel over IR goggles. But if you are only using jyhad cards, an IR Goggle
or two wont hurt, especially if you play with a few freak drives. There is
nothing as sad for a combat deck as having your fistfull of devastating
combat cards defeated by one simple card.

Floatey.

begining to be played with no card limit. Jyhad doesn't use a card limit as a
balancing factor, and the official rules (tournament or no) call for no card
limits.

If you like using only 4 of each card, by all means, do so, but don't make the
mistake of coming in to Jyhad thinking you should automaticaly be using a 4
card limit because there is one in Magic. They are different games.
